description: Slot A as narrowed by A10: calibration retained for the textually demonstrable half, origin edge undetermined between rivals. PILOT. Every document here is the origin or a correction. The propagators are now IDENTIFIED -- not from Vreeman & Carroll's w-list, which stayed behind a CAPTCHA, but from Valtin's own reference list, which is better because Valtin QUOTES them (refs 3, 17, 42, 54). They are still absent as nodes because every propagator excerpt available is RELAYED through Valtin, and only HELD is committable. Results demonstrate the pipeline and A6's confound, and demonstrate nothing about calibration.

sources.citation: Food and Nutrition Board, National Academy of Sciences. Recommended Dietary Allowances, revised 1945. National Research Council, Reprint and Circular Series No. 122, 1945 (Aug), pp. 3-18.
Valtin, Heinz. "'Drink at least eight glasses of water a day.' Really?" American Journal of Physiology 283, no. 5 (2002): R993-R1004.
sources.role: investigation; reports the FNB origin at two removes and floats a SECOND, rival origin it then argues against

sources.citation: Vreeman, Rachel C., and Aaron E. Carroll. "Medical myths." BMJ 335, no. 7633 (22 December 2007): 1288-1289. Not commissioned; not externally peer reviewed.
Carroll, Aaron E. "No, You Do Not Have to Drink 8 Glasses of Water a Day." The New York Times (The Upshot), 24 August 2015. Print version 25 August 2015, Section A, p. 3, under a different headline.
sources.role: correction; cites Valtin by hyperlink, never by name

spans.text: Most of this quantity is contained in prepared foods.
A suitable allowance of water for adults is 2.5 liters daily in most instances.
spans.note: Stops at two documents: vreeman2007 carries the British 'litres' and 'millilitre'. That difference is the mutation; absorbing it into the span would erase it.

spans.text: Water should be allowed ad libitum, since sensations of thirst usually serve as adequate guides to intake except for infants and sick persons.
spans.note: Attested in ONE document. Neither Valtin nor Vreeman & Carroll quote this sentence. The weakest excerpt in slot A, and the one carrying the second deletion.
The rival origin's text, and it survives BOTH the web and print editions of vreeman2007 unchanged -- which is why the print variant does not break this span.

spans.text: in the form of coffee, tea, milk, soft drinks, beer, etc.
spans.note: The clause that DEFEATS the rival origin: Stare allowed the caffeinated drinks 8x8 forbids. Both investigators quote it, and neither propagator does.

asserted_descents.note: Reported at TWO REMOVES and now fully cited: Valtin ref 65 is Papai J, 'Eight glasses of water per day. An update', urbanlegends.com, and Papai relays P. Thomas, who is never cited at all. Valtin states the mechanism -- the last sentence of the FNB passage 'was not heeded' -- which is why `thirst_qualifier` and `prepared_foods` matter. The downstream endpoint, the propagated claim, is ABSENT from this corpus, so the edge cannot form (A9). cited_by is EXPLICIT: the default -- every instance of the asserting document -- silently gave this assertion two endpoints once A.valtin2002.q_stare existed, both in valtin2002, so it formed no edge AND dropped out of unresolved_assertions. An assertion that vanishes is the precise failure A9 was written to prevent, and the default reintroduced it the moment a second locus was added.

The RIVAL origin, and the one A10 said the corpus lacked. Valtin ref 81 is Stare FJ & McWilliams M, `Nutrition for Good Health`, Plycon, Fullerton CA, 1974, p. 175 -- reached not by search but through an OBITUARY (ref 77) and a former colleague (ref 82). Valtin quotes the passage in full, then gives four numbered reasons against it: undocumented, '6 to 8' is not 'at least eight', it ALLOWS caffeinated drinks, and it credits the regulation 8x8 denies. So the asserting document argues against its own assertion -- an edge no arm should draw with confidence. Upstream endpoint ABSENT: the Stare passage is RELAYED through Valtin, never HELD (A9).

'One origin may be a 1945 recommendation' (w5), with the mechanism at w6: 'If the last, crucial sentence is ignored...'. A SECOND document asserting the same undetermined edge, five years after Valtin, and hedged the same way. Downstream endpoint still absent (A9).

'Another endorsement may have come from' (w7). Both investigators reached both candidates and neither picked one, which is the strongest evidence slot A has that the origin edge is genuinely undetermined rather than merely unresearched. Upstream endpoint absent (A9).

key_authoring_note.rule: Record ONLY the highest-precedence mutation operator for each edge. An edge can genuinely carry several -- slot A has one that is both an attribution shift and a deletion -- but `mutation` is single-valued (A13), and a key recording both would count one as `misidentified` against an arm that was entirely correct.
precedence: deletion -- the descendant's sentences are a proper subset of the ancestor's
rewording -- the excerpts differ and nothing above applies
none -- the excerpts are identical modulo whitespace and case

expect.note: Structural only. No expected edge, support kind or mutation appears here -- those live in key_A.json, authored by hand and separately (FR-2).

known_gaps: Propagators: ROLE held from vreeman2007's body text ('found throughout the popular press.w1-w4') and CITATIONS held from Valtin's list (3 = UCLA S-N-A-C pamphlet 2000; 17 = Brody, NY Times, 11 July 2000, p. D8; 42 = Hines, Am Fitness 19:23-25, 2001; 54 = Majette-Haynes, IBWA). They are still NOT NODES: every propagator sentence available is relayed through Valtin, and only HELD is committable. The bmj.com w-list, which would give w1-w4's own identities, is behind a CAPTCHA and was not obtained.

stare1974 itself not obtained. The rival origin now has textual substance -- two HELD documents quote it -- but the quoted document is absent, so both Stare assertions have an absent upstream endpoint.
One locus is §unresolved (carroll2015, which has no pagination to resolve). fnb1945's page within pp. 3-18 and valtin2002's page within R993-R1004 are section-resolved only.
thirst_qualifier is attested in one document and corroborated by nothing.

vreeman2007 exists in TWO editions that differ inside slot A's own excerpts, and the corpus treats them as one source. Held as a decision, not an oversight: promoting the print run to its own source_id would add a fourth reading of the millilitre clause and a same-document pair the mechanism must decline. The key author owns that call, and carroll2015 has the identical fork.
